question: The Great Bath found at Mohenjo-daro was a large:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectangular tank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath is one of the most famous structures among the ruins of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization city of Mohenjo-daro in Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• It is a large rectangular tank, measuring approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep.
 
• The Great Bath is made with finely fitted bricks and was likely used for ritualistic or religious purposes.
 
• The bath was waterproofed with a thick layer of bitumen (natural tar) to ensure water retention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-daro**

 
 
• Mohenjo-daro, meaning "Mound of the Dead Men," is an ancient Indus Valley Civilization city that dates back to 2500 BCE.
 
• It is one of the largest settlements of the ancient civilization and one of the world's earliest major urban centers.
 
• The city was discovered in the 1920s and is located in the Larkana District of Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• Mohenjo-daro features advanced urban planning, including streets laid out in a grid pattern, a sophisticated drainage system, and the use of standardized fired bricks for construction.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was a Bronze Age civilization that flourished in the northwestern regions of South Asia from 3300 to 1300 BCE.
 
• It is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Key sites of the civilization include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
• The civilization had a writing system, though its script has not yet been deciphered.
 
 
 
• **Ritualistic Practices**
 
 
• The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is believed to have been used for religious or ritualistic purposes, possibly for purification rites.
 
• Such ritualistic bathing practices are seen in many ancient cultures and are often associated with spiritual cleansing.
 
• The presence of a well and a drainage system near the bath suggests that water management was an important aspect of these practices.
